title: The Indifferent Desert
working_title: The Indifferent Desert (chosen — a DISTINCT title; Martin's in-copyright memoir holds 'The Sheltering Desert')
based_on: the true story of Henno Martin & Hermann Korn (orig. memoir 'The Sheltering Desert', 1956) — ORIGINAL RETELLING of the EVENTS, not a derivative of the in-copyright text
protagonist: Henno Martin (close-third) + Hermann Korn (co-lead, seen from outside) + Otto the dog
setting: the Namib / the Kuiseb River canyon, South-West Africa, 1940-1942 (+ a 1946/post coda)
logline: Two German geologists who read rock and water for a living walk away from a war that would cage them and into the one place that might kill them faster — and learn that the desert they thought they understood as scientists will only let them live if they let it teach them how, one hunger and one waterhole at a time.
blueprint: survival-and-friendship literary novel (refuses to be an adventure) — descent → building a life → the diet crisis (midpoint) → attrition → Korn's beriberi → surrender → the strange anticlimax
market: unsentimental survival/desert literature (the Sheltering Desert itself, honoured not copied; van der Post; Endurance) + the project's grounded-Africa eye
tone: great real bushcraft; not always a fun read; real story; real respect
dedication: Ferdie — Okahandja / Namib; Chobe brother; full profile in canon/APPENDIX.md
clearances: both men long deceased (Korn 1946, Martin 1998) → depictable; the BOOK is in copyright (EU life+70 → 2068) → original retelling of facts only, never a derivative of Martin's prose
sensitivity_read: REQUIRED before publication — Namibian/German-Namibian history; Namib natural history (Gobabeb); the Topnaar (ǂAonin) representation; restraint on Korn's ambiguous 1946 death
